definitions.explanation: The larger group in a division of opinion, votes, or affiliation. Used in politics, group dynamics, and general discussions about which side has more support.

examples.japanese: {多数派|たすうは}の{意見|いけん}が{通|とお}った。
{議会|ぎかい}では{与党|よとう}が{多数派|たすうは}を{占|し}めている。
examples.english: The ruling party holds the majority in the parliament.

examples.japanese: {多数派|たすうは}に{属|ぞく}していなくても、{自分|じぶん}の{意見|いけん}をしっかり{持|も}つことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to hold firm to your own opinion even if you don't belong to the majority.

notes:
{多数派|たすうは} is a compound of {多数|たすう} (many, majority) and {派|は} (faction, group).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多数派|たすうは}を{占|し}める: to hold the majority
- {多数派|たすうは}の{意見|いけん}: majority opinion
- {多数派|たすうは}に{属|ぞく}する: to belong to the majority
- {多数派|たすうは}{工作|こうさく}: majority-building maneuvering (political)

ANTONYM:
- {少数派|しょうすうは}: minority, minority faction

REGISTER:
Common in political, social, and academic discussions. In everyday conversation, {多|おお}い{方|ほう} or みんな might be used instead.
